magic_items.name: +1 Longsword (Talon)
magic_items.description: The chest also holds a +1 longsword in a silver-chased scabbard. The sword is inscribed with the name "Talon," and its hilt is worked in the shape of a bird of prey with outspread wings. It once belonged to a great knight named Aldith Tresendar, known as the Black Hawk. A character who succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence (History) check recognizes the sword and recalls this lore. Sir Aldith died fighting off the ores that attacked through the hidden caverns below his manor. Talon was lost here until the nothic found it.

magic_items.name: Scroll of Augury
magic_items.description: The chest contains 160 sp, 120 gp, five malachite gems (15 gp each), two potions of healing, and a scroll of augury.

magic_items.name: Staff of Defense
magic_items.description:
This slender, hollow staff is made of glass yet is as strong as oak. It weighs 3 pounds.
You must be attuned to the staff to gain its benefits and cast its spells.
While holding the staff, you have a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.
The staff has 10 charges, which are used to fuel the spells within it. With the staff in hand, you can use your action to cast one of the following spells from the staff if the spell is on your class's spell list: mage armor (1 charge) or shield (2 charges). No components are required.
The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges each day at dawn. If you expend the staff's last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff shatters and is destroyed.

magic_items.name: Scroll of Darkness
magic_items.description: A scroll of darkness in a bone tube.

magic_items.name: Hew
magic_items.description: Hew is a +1 battleaxe that deals maximum damage when the wielder hits a plant creature or an object made of wood. The axe's creator was a dwarf smith who feuded with the dryads of a forest where he cut firewood. Whoever carries the axe feels uneasy whenever he or she travels through a forest.

magic_items.name: Gold Statuette of a Sun Elf
magic_items.description: A gold statuette of a sun elf (100 gp) wrapped in crimson cloth. A detect magic spell reveals that the statuette is imbued with divination magic. Any non-evil creature grasping the statue can ask it a question and receive a telepathic response, as though it had cast augury (see the rulebook for a description of this spell). Once a creature has asked its question and received a response, it can never activate the statuette again.

magic_items.name: Potion of Vitality
magic_items.description: Drinking this potion removes any exhaustion you are suffering, cures any disease or poison affecting you, and maximizes the effect of any Hit Die you spend to regain hit points within the next 24 hours.

magic_items.name: Lightbringer
magic_items.description: This +1 mace was made for a cleric of Lathander, the god of dawn. The head of the mace is shaped like a sunburst and made of solid brass. Named Lightbringer, this weapon glows as bright as a torch when its wielder commands. While glowing, the mace deals an extra 1d6 radiant damage to undead creatures.

magic_items.name: Dragonguard
magic_items.description: This +1 breastplate has a gold dragon motif worked into its design. Created for a human hero of Neverwinter named Tergon, it grants its wearer advantage on saving throws against the breath weapons of creatures that have the dragon type.

magic_items.name: Spider Staff
magic_items.description: This staff is carved to resemble a spider. It can be used as a magic quarterstaff. While holding it, you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned, and you have resistance to poison damage. The staff has 10 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: spider climb (1 charge), web (2 charges), or conjure animals (3 charges, spiders only). The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff is destroyed and turns to dust.

magic_items.name: +1 Armor
magic_items.description:
The most basic form of magic armor is a superb product of physical and magical craft. You have a +1 bonus to your Armor Class while wearing this armor.
A suit of +1 armor never rusts or deteriorates, and it magically resizes to fit its wearer.

magic_items.name: +1 Weapon
magic_items.description:
Magic weapons are unmistakably finer in quality than their ordinary counterparts. You have a +1 bonus to the attack rolls and damage rolls you make with this weapon.
Some +1 weapons (swords in particular) have additional properties, such as shedding light.

features.name: Illumination
features.description: The flameskull sheds either dim light in a 15-foot radius, or bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. It can switch between the options as an action.

features.name: Magic Resistance
features.description: The flameskull has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

features.name: Rejuvenation
features.description: If the flameskull is destroyed, it regains all its hit points in 1 hour unless holy water is sprinkled on its remains or a dispel magic or remove curse spell is cast on them.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
The flameskull is a 5th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). It requires no somatic or material components to cast its spells. The flameskull has the following wizard spells prepared:

Cantrips (at will): mage hand
1st level (3 slots): magic missile, shield
2nd level (2 slots): blur, flaming sphere
3rd level (1 slot): fireball

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The flameskull uses Fire Ray twice.

actions.name: Fire Ray
actions.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 30 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (3d6) fire damage.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
The mage is a 4th-level spellcaster that uses Intelligence as its spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13; +5 to hit with spell attacks). The mage knows the following spells from the wizard's spell list:
Cantrips (at will): light, mage hand, shocking grasp
1st Level (4 slots): charm person, magic missile
2nd Level (3 slots): hold person, misty step

actions.name: Quarterstaff
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +1 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d8 - 1) bludgeoning damage.

monsters.name: Mormesk the Wraith
damage_resistances: acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons that aren't silvered

features.name: Incorporeal Movement
features.description: The wraith can move through an object or another creature, but can't stop there.

features.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
features.description: While in sunlight, the wraith has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) necrotic damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. If this attack reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies. This reduction to the target's hit point maximum lasts until the target finishes a long rest.

features.name: Special Equipment
features.description: Nezznar has a spider staff.

features.name: Fey Ancestry
features.description: Nezznar has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put him to sleep.

features.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
features.description: Nezznar has disadvantage on attack rolls when he or his target is in sunlight.

features.name: Innate Spellcasting
features.description:
Nezznar can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:
• At will: dancing lights
• 1/day each: darkness, faerie fire (save DC 12)

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
Nezznar is a 4th-level spellcaster that uses Intelligence as his spellcasting ability (spell save DC 13; +5 to hit with spell attacks). Nezznar has the following spells prepared from the wizard's spell list:
• Cantrips (at will): mage hand, ray of frost, shocking grasp
• 1st Level (4 slots): mage armor, magic missile, shield
• 2nd Level (3 slots): invisibility, suggestion

actions.name: Spider Staff
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +1 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d6 - 1) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) poison damage.

features.name: Keen Sight
features.description: The nothic has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The nothic makes two attacks with its claws.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage.

actions.name: Rotting Gaze
actions.description: The nothic chooses one creature within 30 feet of it that it can see. The target must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw against this magic or take 10 (3d6) necrotic damage.

actions.name: Weird Insight
actions.description: The nothic chooses one creature within 30 feet of it that it can see. The target must contest its Charisma (Deception) check against the nothic's Wisdom (Insight) check. If the nothic wins, it magically learns one fact or secret about the creature.

monsters.name: Twig Blight
monsters.senses: blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius), passive Perception 9

features.name: False Appearance
features.description: The blight resembles a dead shrub. While it remains motionless among vegetation, it can hide without being out of sight.

actions.name: Claws
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

npcs.name: Sildar Hallwinter
npcs.description: Sildar Hallwinter is a kindhearted human male of nearly fifty years who holds a place of honor in the famous griffon cavalry of the great city of Waterdeep. He is an agent of the Lords' Alliance, a group of allied political powers concerned with mutual security and prosperity. Members of the order ensure the safety of cities and other settlements by proactively eliminating threats by any means, while bringing honor and glory to their leaders and homelands. Sildar met Gundren Rockseeker in Neverwinter and agreed to accompany him back to Phandalin. Sildar wants to investigate the fate of Iarno Albrek, a human wizard and fellow member of the Lords' Alliance who disappeared shortly after arriving in Phandalin. Sildar hopes to learn what happened to Iarno, assist Gundren in reopening the old mine, and help restore Phandalin to a civilized center of wealth and prosperity.

npcs.name: Linene Graywind

features.name: Recovered Goods
features.description: If the characters return the stolen goods found in area 8 of the Cragmaw hideout (or if they left the goods but reveal where they can be found), Linene gives them a reward of 50 gp and promises to help the adventurers any way she can.

npcs.description: The master of the Phandalin post is a sharp-tongued human woman of thirty-five named Linene Graywind. She knows that bandits have raided Lionshield caravans, but she doesn't know who is responsible. In a back room, Linene keeps a supply of armor and weapons, all of which are for sale to interested buyers. Linene has a few scruples, however, and won't sell weapons to anyone she thinks might be a threat to the town. Among those with whom she refuses to do business are the Redbrands. She warns the characters that the ruffians are trouble and advises them to avoid the Sleeping Giant tap house.

npcs.name: Halia Thornton

features.name: Quest: Halia's Job Offer
features.description: If approached by characters she believes she can control, Halia explains that the Redbrands are a problem. She tells how the ruffians loiter around the Sleeping Giant tap house and have a base under Tresendar Manor, on the east edge of town. She then offers the characters 100 gp to eliminate the Redbrand leader, whom the outlaws call Glasstaff, and bring her any correspondence found in the leader's quarters. Halia doesn't reveal that she wants to take over the Redbrand operation herself. A DC 15 Wisdom (Insight) check indicates she has ulterior motives for wanting the Redbrand leader dead.

npcs.description: The guildmaster is an ambitious and calculating human woman named Halia Thornton. In her attempts to establish the Miner's Exchange as the closest thing the town has to a governing authority, she acts as more than a simple merchant. She is also an agent of the Zhentarim, a powerful organization that seeks to exert secret control over the North through wealth and influence. Halia is working slowly to bring Phandalin under her control, and can become a valuable patron to the characters if they don't cross her. Halia doesn't know the location of Cragmaw Castle, but she has heard that the Redbrands have a goblin minion serving them. She suggests the goblin might know the location. She leverages this information to try to persuade the characters into helping her deal with the Redbrands.

npcs.name: Droop

features.name: Cowardly
features.description: He is such a coward that if he is ordered to fight, he does so with disadvantage (as explained in the rulebook).

npcs.description: The goblin, Droop, is not a threat to the party. He has been cowed by the bugbears and follows their orders until someone stronger comes along. If he regains consciousness during combat, Droop hides and avoids the fight. Droop knows the general layout of the Redbrand hideout, as well as the location of its secret doors and traps. He doesn't think to offer up the information, but if prompted, he reveals as much as he can remember in an attempt to be useful to the party. Some of the details might be confusing or mixed up. He is a goblin, after all. If the bugbears are dispatched, Droop tries to ingratiate himself with the party. He doesn't remember the route to Cragmaw Castle, but he knows it's up north, in the forest. He also knows that Cragmaw goblins patrol around Phandalin, and he suggests the characters might be able to capture a patrol to learn more about the castle.

npcs.name: Mosk

features.name: Eye Patch
features.description: He wears a jeweled eye patch even though he has both his eyes. Mosk wears the eye patch because he thinks it's fancy.

equipment: eye patch made of black leather set with semiprecious stones (50 gp)
iron key that locks and unlocks all the doors in the Redbrand hideout
npcs.description: The leader of the bugbears is named Mosk. He wears a jeweled eye patch even though he has both his eyes. Mosk wears the eye patch because he thinks it's fancy. The bugbears work for the Black Spider and were sent here to help Iarno keep the Redbrands and the citizens of Phandalin in line.

npcs.name: Iarno Albrek

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: Iarno uses his staff of defense to cast mage armor on himself. He then casts offensive spells at enemies he can see. Iarno's stat block contains a list of the spells he has prepared. For descriptions of those spells and their effects, see the rule book. Iarno uses the shield power of his staff for added protection.

npcs.description: A former member of the Lords' Alliance, Iarno seized an opportunity in Phandalin to line his own pockets. Originally tasked with setting up a constabulary, the mage instead assembled a group of outlaws and local ruffians to secure his own position in town. Iarno knew of the Black Spider through his contacts in the Lords' Alliance and brokered a meeting. The drow promised to share the secrets and wealth of the Forge of Spells with the wizard in exchange for his help and loyalty. Iarno puts on airs of gentility and courteous manners, addressing his ruffians as "my good gentlemen," and referring to sordid acts such as kidnapping or arson as "that unpleasant little business" or "those unfortunate events." He refers to the characters as "guests" and expresses regret that he cannot provide suitable entertainment for their visit. Beneath his genteel demeanor, however, Iarno is just as thuggish and arrogant as any Redbrand outlaws.

npcs.name: Hamun Kost

features.name: Necromantic Tattoo
features.description: Kost is a stout, red-robed figure with sallow skin, a shaved scalp, and a black tattoo on his forehead. A character who succeeds on a DC 10 Intelligence (Arcana) check recognizes Kost's tattoo as a necromantic symbol. A successful DC 10 Intelligence (History) check verifies the garb as that usual for Thay, a land far to the east where wizards pattern their flesh with tattoos. The tattoo on the head represents a wizard's school of magic. Kost's school is necromancy.

npcs.description: Hamun Kost is an evil mage (Red Wizard of Thay) who is busy exploring Old Owl Well in the hope of gleaning arcane lore left behind by its builders. He is not particularly aggressive and is willing to strike a deal that advances his interests at the same time it helps the characters.

npcs.name: Agatha

features.name: Divination
features.description: Agatha is well informed and a capable diviner, so she can answer almost any single question pertaining to the adventure that the characters think to ask. However, the banshee answers only one question, so the characters should choose it carefully.

npcs.description: The ghostly figure smiles with cold amusement. She is a banshee who traded Bowgentle's spellbook to a necromancer named Tsernoth from the city of Iriaebor more than a hundred years ago.

npcs.name: Yegg
npcs.description: A fat, cantankerous goblin with 12 hit points named Yegg. Yegg is the chief cook for the Cragmaws, and he viciously bullies his unwilling assistants as they go about the work of putting food on the tribe's table. If Yegg is killed, any goblins left alive flee to the east or west, avoiding the north door because of the trap in area 2.

npcs.name: Lhupo
npcs.description: Lhupo (a goblin with 12 hit points) and two ordinary goblins that serve as his 'acolytes.' They all wear filthy robes over their armor, but none of them possess divine powers (although Lhupo claims to hear Maglubiyet speaking to him).

npcs.name: King Grol
npcs.description: King Grol is a fierce old bugbear with 45 hit points. He rules the Cragmaws through pure intimidation. Age has stooped his shoulders and hunched his back, but he remains surprisingly agile and strong. He is demanding and vindictive, and no Cragmaw dares to cross him.

npcs.name: Snarl
npcs.description: Snarl is a wolf with 18 hit points, attending King Grol.

npcs.name: Vyerith
npcs.description: Vyerith is a doppelganger disguised as a female drow, a messenger from the Black Spider, come to collect Gundren Rockseeker and the map of Wave Echo Cave from King Grol.

npcs.name: Gundren Rockseeker
npcs.description: Gundren Rockseeker is a dwarf commoner. He is unconscious but stable at 0 hit points.

npcs.name: Targor Bloodsword
npcs.description: Targor Bloodsword is a hobgoblin with 20 hit points who leads a returning war band. He has long aspired to lead the Cragmaw tribe.

npcs.name: Nezznar the Black Spider
equipment: iron key with a head shaped like an anvil
npcs.description: Nezznar is the Black Spider, a drow who uses the Cragmaw goblins and the Redbrands to keep Wave Echo Cave secret. He is curious about the characters and will betray them as soon as they outlive their usefulness.

npcs.name: Nundro Rockseeker
npcs.description: Nundro is a dwarf commoner and the youngest of the three Rockseeker brothers. He was captured by Nezznar and interrogated harshly. He is grateful if rescued and offers to tag along.

traps.name: Snare
traps.trigger: A character who fails to notice the trap triggers the snare.

detection.detail: If the characters are searching for traps, the character in the lead spots the trap automatically if his or her passive Wisdom (Perception) score is 12 or higher. Otherwise, the character must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check to notice the trap.

disarm.detail: The character is restrained until 1 or more slashing damage is dealt to the snare's cord.

traps.effect: The character is suspended upside down 10 feet above the ground. The character is restrained until 1 or more slashing damage is dealt to the snare's cord. A character who isn't carefully lowered down takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.
traps.description: A hidden snare on the goblin trail that suspends a character upside down.

traps.name: Pit
traps.trigger: The pit triggers when a creature moves across it.

detection.detail: The character in the lead spots the hidden pit automatically if his or her passive Wisdom (Perception) score is 15 or higher. Otherwise, the character must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to spot the hidden pit.

traps.effect: The lead character must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall in, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage. The pit's walls are not steep, so no ability check is required to scramble out.
traps.description: A camouflaged pit on the goblin trail.

traps.name: Fragile Ledge
traps.trigger: Any weight in excess of 100 pounds on the ledge between the two escarpments

detection.detail: Not explicitly stated; the ledge is described as fragile.

disarm.detail: Not applicable; it is a natural hazard.

traps.effect: The whole mass loosens and tumbles down to the east. Any creature on the ledge when it falls must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage on a failure, or half as much damage on a success. The creature also falls prone on a failed save.
traps.area: The ledge between the two escarpments in the western passage
traps.description: A fragile ledge that collapses under excessive weight, sending creatures tumbling down.

traps.name: Flood!
traps.trigger: The goblins in area 7 are signaled by the lookout in area 5 and knock away the supports, releasing a surge of water.

detection.detail: Not explicitly stated; the flood is a sudden event.

disarm.detail: Not applicable; it is a triggered trap.

traps.effect: A water surge pours from area 7 down to area 1. Any creature within 10 feet of the disused passage at area 4 or the steps leading up to area 3 can attempt a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw to avoid being swept away. A creature that fails to get out of the way can attempt a DC 15 Strength saving throw to hold on. On a failed save, the character is knocked prone and washed down to area 1, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage along the way.
traps.area: The main passage from area 7 down to area 1, specifically within 10 feet of the disused passage at area 4 or the steps leading up to area 3.
traps.description: A trap that releases a surge of water down the main passage of the lair.

traps.name: Hidden Pit Trap
traps.trigger: The tiles and timbers collapse under 100 or more pounds of weight.

detection.detail: A character searching the hall for traps can spot the covered pit with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. A successful check also reveals narrow ledges on the north and south sides of the pit.

disarm.detail: No disarm method is described in the source text.

traps.effect: A creature that triggers the trap or fails the Dexterity check to skirt around the edge of the pit must attempt a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw to catch the edge. On a failed save, the creature falls 20 feet to the dirt floor of the pit, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and landing prone.
traps.area: The pit trap is in the middle of the hallway, hidden under a false floor consisting of loose stone tiles laid atop breakaway timbers. The pit is 20 feet deep.
traps.description: A hidden pit trap in a hallway, covered by a false floor that collapses under 100 or more pounds of weight.

traps.name: Pit Trap
traps.trigger: A creature that fails the Dexterity check to skirt around the edge of the pit
traps.effect: The creature must attempt a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw to catch the edge. On a failed save, the creature falls 20 feet to the dirt floor of the pit, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and landing prone.
traps.description: A pit trap that drops a creature 20 feet onto a dirt floor.

traps.name: Collapsing Bridge
traps.trigger: A creature weighing more than 50 pounds moves across the south bridge.

detection.detail: A character next to the bridge can discern that the construction is faulty with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

disarm.method: Any creature can use an action to dislodge one end of either bridge, dropping it into the crevasse.
disarm.detail: Any creature can use an action to dislodge one end of either bridge, dropping it into the crevasse.

traps.effect: The south bridge collapses when a creature weighing more than 50 pounds moves across it, dropping the creature into the crevasse.
traps.area: The south wooden bridge spanning the crevasse.
traps.description: The south bridge is rigged to collapse when a creature weighing more than 50 pounds moves across it.

traps.name: Crevasse
traps.trigger: A creature falls into the crevasse.

detection.detail: The crevasse is an open fissure, 5 to 10 feet wide and 20 feet deep, easily visible.

traps.effect: A creature that falls into the crevasse takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage and lands prone in a jumble of rubble that is difficult terrain. The bottom of the crevasse feels unnaturally cold. When viewed with a detect magic spell, the area emanates a faint necromantic aura. The magic causes all organic matter in the crevasse to age and decompose at half the normal rate.
traps.area: A steep-sided fissure 5 to 10 feet wide and 20 feet deep.
traps.description: A steep-sided fissure in the cavern floor that damages and knocks prone creatures that fall in, and magically ages organic matter at half the normal rate.

traps.name: Cave-In Trap
traps.trigger: Any creature that walks over or through the rubble without avoiding the tripwire triggers a cave-in of wooden beams and heavy stones.

detection.detail: Spotting the tripwire requires a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of at least 20, or a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check if characters are actively searching for traps in the area.

disarm.detail: Once spotted, the tripwire is easily avoided and disarmed (no ability check required).

traps.effect: A cave-in of wooden beams and heavy stones. Any creature in the area when the trap triggers must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage from the falling rubble (half as much damage on a successful save). The noise of the collapse puts the monsters in areas 3, 7, 8, and 9 on alert.
traps.area: The area of the collapse is marked on the map.
traps.description: A copper tripwire connected to linchpins hidden in the ruined ceiling, concealed by dusty plaster and rubble in front of the door leading to area 8.

traps.name: Trap in Area 2
traps.trigger: Unknown (referenced but not detailed in this text)
traps.effect: Unknown (referenced but not detailed in this text)
traps.description: A trap located in area 2 of the Cragmaw Castle. Goblins avoid the north door of the banquet hall because of this trap.

traps.name: Poison Gas
traps.trigger: Whenever a creature attempts to cross the cavern, the carpets of fungi that cover most of the floor release poisonous gas into the air.

detection.detail: The glowing fungi allow creatures to see the entire cavern without the aid of darkvision or a light source.

traps.effect: Each creature in the cavern must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or take 3d6 poison damage and be poisoned for 10 minutes. The gas disperses after 1 minute, but until then, any living creature that ends its turn in the cavern must repeat the saving throw.
traps.description: A cavern covered in glowing fungi that release poisonous gas when creatures attempt to cross.

traps.name: Ceiling Collapse (Temple of Dumathoin)
traps.trigger: Removing either emerald eye from the statue of Dumathoin

detection.detail: Close inspection and a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals the jewels are clever fakes made of worthless glass. A detect magic spell reveals a strong aura of abjuration magic surrounding the statue.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified; the trap is triggered by removing a jewel.

traps.effect: The pillars that line the walls crack, triggering a ceiling collapse. Each creature in the room must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A magical trap protecting the fake emerald eyes of the statue of Dumathoin. Removing either eye causes the pillars to crack and the ceiling to collapse.

traps.name: Ceiling Collapse
traps.trigger: Removing either jewel eye from the statue

detection.detail: A detect magic spell reveals a strong aura of abjuration magic surrounding the statue.

traps.effect: The pillars that line the walls crack, triggering a ceiling collapse. Each creature in the room must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 bludgeoning damage from falling rubble and falling prone on a failure, or taking only half the damage on a success.
traps.description: A trap that causes the ceiling to collapse when either jewel eye is removed from a statue.
